rows.title: Procedural Interference Score as a Predictor of Negative Transfer in Memory-Augmented Agents
rows.exact_prediction: For xBench tasks where Cheatsheet or Voyager is used, the procedural interference score (defined as a measure of discrepancy between the retrieved skill's executable procedure and the task's required step sequence) will predict a negative transfer event (performance below the no-memory baseline) with AUC > 0.7 on a held-out set, and this AUC will be statistically significantly higher than a same-information conflict-detection baseline and a same-information utilization-diagnostic baseline.
rows.strongest_same_information_baseline: A conflict-detection baseline that flags retrieved memories containing explicit contradiction markers (supersedes, contradicts, applicability-boundary violations) relative to the task requirements, receiving the same retrieved memory, task requirements, and retrieval confidence as the interference score.
rows.falsifier_expression: Run a controlled comparison on xBench with Cheatsheet and Voyager: (1) oracle-load the retrieved memory (force utilization), (2) compute the proposed procedural interference score on each instance, (3) compute a same-information conflict-detection baseline on the same instances, (4) measure whether the score predicts negative transfer with higher AUC than the baseline. If not, the score is reduced.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The interference score must be defined as a pre-outcome measure (computable from retrieved memory + task requirements alone, before observing the agent's trajectory or outcome). Post-hoc trajectory geometry or endpoint-leaking features are not admissible.

rows.title: Information-Set Dependence of Irrecoverable Contamination Loss in Self-Evolving Skill Pools
rows.exact_prediction: Under a preregistered information-set sweep on the released Terminal-Bench 2 skill pools from arXiv:2608.05810, the recovery curve indexed by information kind (source identity < +descendant text < +embedding state < full activation trace) will either be flat at 5.6pp irrecoverable (falsifying the P+M axes) or non-flat (supporting them). A non-flat curve with a strictly positive sub-component unlocked by information beyond source identity is the cheapest positive result.
rows.strongest_same_information_baseline: The existing Oracle protocol in arXiv:2608.05810 Figure 4, extended to be a multi-level oracle stratified by information kind, run on the same Terminal-Bench 2 tasks and same released R1–R5 skill pools.
rows.falsifier_expression: On the released arXiv:2608.05810 Terminal-Bench 2 R5 skill pool, run a 4-level information-set sweep: (L0) source-identity-only oracle, (L1) + distilled text of descendants, (L2) + embedding centroids of descendants, (L3) full Oracle as in Figure 4. Measure recovery at each level on the same held-out task set. If recovery is constant across L0–L3 (within noise), the 5.6pp is information-invariant and the P+M axes collapse. If recovery increases by a practically large amount from L0 to L3, the P+M axes survive. This is implementable from the primary source's released artifacts at zero method-development cost.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: Branch requires headroom on the recovery axis (the 5.6pp is the unresolved headroom) and on the information-set axis (no curve is published); both are pre-existing headroom in the primary source's own measurement, not new degrees of freedom introduced by the branch.

rows.title: Cross-Round Contamination Irreversibility Boundary: A 5.6pp Irrecoverable Performance Residual Under Oracle Cleanup
rows.exact_prediction: Under oracle cleanup (perfect information about all contaminating skills and their full descendant lineages), a measurable performance residual of 5.6pp ± noise will persist, and this residual will scale with the number of distillation rounds (R), not with the size of the contaminating skill set alone.
rows.strongest_same_information_baseline: AGM belief contraction + standard unlearning + iterated self-distillation persistence: the best same-information model is one that combines full belief contraction under oracle information, complete descendant lineage removal, and a distillation-persistence bound that accounts for path-dependence. If this combined model predicts zero residual and the 5.6pp persists, the candidate survives.
rows.falsifier_expression: Re-run the source paper's experiment (Ungated skill accumulation on Terminal-Bench 2) with an additional condition: after R5, condition the skill-generation operator on the *full pre-R1 trajectory history* (not just the current skill pool) and measure whether the 5.6pp residual collapses. If it does, the residual is explained by same-information history-dependence and the candidate is reduced. If it persists, the candidate survives. This is a zero-authority evidence-acquisition falsifier.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The candidate is not a gating method (VaG exists); it is a boundary object. The contribution is the formalization of the boundary, the protocol for measuring it, and the prediction about its scaling. The 'headroom' is in the theory (what determines the 5.6pp magnitude and how to predict it before accumulation) and the benchmark (a standardized irreversibility decomposition protocol).
